body:
## Summary

Prefer the matching object variant when coercing config form values through `anyOf` / `oneOf` unions.

## Problem

`coerceFormValues()` previously recursed into the first object variant it encountered for object-valued unions. In schemas that distinguish object variants using `const` discriminator fields, this could coerce nested values using the wrong variant.

For example, a value like `{ kind: "named", retries: "03" }` could be coerced using a preceding `numeric` variant and incorrectly turn `retries` into `3`.

## Changes

- prefer object variants whose top-level property `const` constraints match the current value- fall back to the first object variant only when no discriminator match exists- add regression tests for both `anyOf` and `oneOf` object unions

## Notes

This keeps coercion behavior unchanged for string/number/boolean unions while making object-union coercion more accurate for discriminated schemas.

author: betegon
body:
Companion to **[getsentry/cli-init-api#114](https://github.com/getsentry/cli-init-api/pull/114)** — the server-side rewrite. Read the server PR first; this one focuses on the client side.

## TL;DR

Replaces the old Mastra-driven CLI flow (`wizard-runner.ts`, `workflow-inputs.ts`) with a thin NDJSON consumer that talks to the new Nitro server. The CLI is now:

- a stream consumer (NDJSON over `GET /api/init/{runId}/stream`),
- a tool dispatcher (executes tool requests against the user's local FS / shell),
- a renderer (clack prompts + spinner + final summary).

All AI work happens server-side. Feature selection moves from a hardcoded upfront prompt to an agent-driven `propose_features` call.

- 21 files changed, **+1,443 / -1,886** (net **−443 LOC**).
- 63 init-related tests pass.

## Glossary (reviewers new to this stack)

- **NDJSON** stream: each line is one JSON event. The CLI fetches `/api/init/{runId}/stream` and dispatches events by `type`.
- **Action**: a request from the workflow for the CLI to do something locally — execute a tool (`list-dir`, `apply-patchset`, …), prompt the user (multi-select, confirm), etc. Each action has a unique `actionId`; the CLI POSTs the result back to `/api/init/actions/{actionId}`.
- **Bridge**: the inverse path. Tools running in the Vercel Sandbox bridge over to the CLI through the workflow. Reviewers don't need to think about it from the CLI side — just know that an `action_request` event on the stream means \"run this locally and post the result back\".

## Architecture (CLI viewpoint)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant CLI as init-runner.ts
  participant Server as Nitro server
  participant Loop as stream + dispatch loop

  User->>CLI: sentry init [./dir] [--features ...]
  CLI->>CLI: preflight (auth, org, team, project, DSN)
  CLI->>Server: POST /api/init {input}
  Server-->>CLI: 202 {runId}
  CLI->>Server: GET /api/init/{runId}/stream

  loop NDJSON events
    Server-->>Loop: status / action_request / summary / done
    alt status
      Loop->>User: spinner.message(...)
    else action_request kind=tool
      Loop->>Loop: executeTool(name, params, cwd)
      Loop->>Server: POST /api/init/actions/{actionId} {ok, output}
    else action_request kind=prompt
      Loop->>User: clack multiselect / confirm
      Loop->>Server: POST /api/init/actions/{actionId} {features}
    else summary
      Loop->>Loop: state.finalOutput = output
    else done
      Loop->>User: formatResult / formatError
    end
  end
```

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`src/lib/init/init-runner.ts`](src/lib/init/init-runner.ts) | Entry runner: preflight → start → stream → dispatch. Replaces `wizard-runner.ts`. |
| [`src/lib/init/transport.ts`](src/lib/init/transport.ts) | `fetch` helpers: `startInit`, `openInitStream`, `resumeInitAction`. |
| [`src/lib/init/stream-parser.ts`](src/lib/init/stream-parser.ts) | `readNdjsonStream` + zod-validated `InitEvent` types. |
| [`src/lib/init/interactive.ts`](src/lib/init/interactive.ts) | Maps `prompt_request` events to clack multiselect / select / confirm. |
| [`src/lib/init/select-features.ts`](src/lib/init/select-features.ts) | `FEATURE_LABELS` + `normaliseFromFlag` for the `--features` override. **No upfront prompt anymore.** |
| [`src/lib/init/ensure-project.ts`](src/lib/init/ensure-project.ts) | Preflight: create / look up a Sentry project so the workflow gets a real DSN. |
| [`src/lib/init/types.ts`](src/lib/init/types.ts) | `InitEvent`, `InitStartInput`, `InitActionRequestEvent`, etc. — wire-format types shared with the server. |

## Code snippets

### 1. Entry: starting the run

```typescript
// src/lib/init/init-runner.ts
const context = await resolveInitContext(opts);                // auth + org + team + project
const project = await ensureSentryProject(context);            // get / create project + DSN
const overrideFeatures = normaliseFromFlag(context.features);  // optional --features override

const startInput: InitStartInput = {
  directory,
  yes,
  dryRun,
  ...(overrideFeatures.length > 0 ? { features: overrideFeatures } : {}),
  org: project.orgSlug,
  team: project.teamSlug,
  project: project.projectSlug,
  existingProject: { /* slug, id, dsn, url */ },
  sentryAuthToken: context.authToken,
  cliVersion: CLI_VERSION,
};

const started = await startInit(startInput, { baseUrl: INIT_API_URL });  // POST /api/init
```

There is no upfront feature prompt. The agent decides which features apply after inspecting the repo. `--features` remains an override for CI / non-interactive use.

### 2. The stream loop with reconnect

```typescript
// src/lib/init/init-runner.ts
async function consumeStreamUntilTerminal({ runId, ... }) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (true) {
    try {
      const stream = await openInitStream(runId, {
        baseUrl: INIT_API_URL,
        startIndex: state.nextStartIndex,    // resume mid-run after disconnects
      });
      for await (const event of readNdjsonStream(stream)) {
        await handleEvent(event, ...);
        if (event.type === \"done\") return;
      }
    } catch (err) {
      if (++attempt >= MAX_STREAM_RECONNECTS) throw err;
      await sleep(1000 * 2 ** attempt);    // exponential backoff
    }
  }
}
```

Bun/undici's `fetch` body has an idle timeout that kills long-lived streams. We accept that and reconnect at the same `startIndex` so we resume mid-run without dropping events.

### 3. Dispatching an action

```typescript
// src/lib/init/init-runner.ts
async function handleEvent(event: InitEvent, ...) {
  state.nextStartIndex += 1;

  if (event.type === \"action_request\") {
    const result = event.kind === \"tool\"
      ? await executeTool(event.name, event.payload, cwd)        // existing CLI tools
      : await handleInteractive(event.payload, { yes, dryRun }); // clack prompts

    await resumeInitAction(event.actionId, { ok: true, output: result });
  }
  if (event.type === \"summary\") state.finalOutput = event.output;
  if (event.type === \"done\")    state.done = event;
}
```

`executeTool` reuses the existing `.cli/` tools (read, glob, run-command, apply-patchset, etc.) so the agent's MCP calls map 1:1 to functions we already trust.

### 4. The agent-driven feature picker (no upfront prompt)

```typescript
// src/lib/init/interactive.ts (multi-select handler)
async function handleMultiSelect(payload: MultiSelectPayload, options: InteractiveContext) {
  const available = payload.availableFeatures ?? [];
  const optional = sortFeatures(available.filter((f) => f !== REQUIRED_FEATURE));

  const selected = await multiselect({
    message: `${payload.prompt}\\n${hints.join(\"\\n\")}`,
    options: optional.map((id) => ({
      value: id,
      label: FEATURE_LABELS[id]?.label ?? id,
      hint: FEATURE_LABELS[id]?.hint,
    })),
    required: false,
  });
  // ...
}
```

The `availableFeatures` list comes from the server's `propose_features` MCP call — the agent has already filtered features that don't apply (e.g. no Session Replay on a server-only Node app). The CLI just renders labels.

## UX before / after

### Before (PR base)
```
◆ Select Sentry features to enable. Error monitoring is always on.
│  ◻ Performance Monitoring (Tracing)
│  ◻ Logging
│  ◻ Session Replay              ← shown even if user has no UI
│  ◻ Profiling
│  ◻ AI Agent Monitoring         ← shown even with no AI deps
│  ◻ User Feedback               ← shown even on a server-only app
│  ◻ Source Maps
│  ◻ Cron Monitoring             ← shown even with no scheduled jobs
```
The agent then has to ignore the user's irrelevant picks.

### After (this PR)
```
◇ Connecting to wizard...
◇ Detecting platform...
◇ Researching Sentry docs...

◆ Select the Sentry features to enable for this project. Error monitoring is always on.
│  Error monitoring is always included
│  space=toggle, a=all, enter=confirm
│  ◻ Performance Monitoring (Tracing)
│  ◻ Logging
│  ◻ Session Replay
│  ◻ Profiling
│  ◻ User Feedback
│  ◻ Source Maps
```

## Summary

Introduces a `type` discriminator on products (`simple` | `variable`) and reshapes the admin create flow to match Shopify/Medusa-style two-phase creation: the user picks a type up-front, the server materializes a default variant for `simple` products, and `variable` products start empty so the user can add options and generate variants on the edit page.

The branch also includes the foundational product CRUD work (forms, options/variants editor, tax-class CRUD, AppDataGrid integration) that this refactor builds on.

## Why this shape

We considered three flows:

1. **Auto-create draft on `/products/new` mount** — orphans drafts on bounce, requires a sentinel tax class because `tax_class_id` is `NOT NULL`, needs cleanup logic.
2. **Two-phase form (chosen)** — local until first save, then redirect to `/products/:id` with the full edit experience unlocked. No orphans, matches Shopify/Medusa.
3. **Hybrid type-picker step** — overkill for two type values.

Option 2 is what the codebase was already evolving toward (the create form already redirects to the edit page on success); this PR formalizes it.

## What changed

### Database (`packages/database`)
- New `productTypeEnum` (`'simple' | 'variable'`) in `00-enums.ts`
- New `type` column on `products` (`NOT NULL`, default `'simple'`) with an index
- **Apply via `pnpm db:push`** — the project's convention is push-based, no generated migration files

### Shared types (`packages/types/src/admin/product.ts`)
- Exports `ProductType`, `productTypeSchema`, `productTypeValues`
- `createProductBody.type` defaults to `'simple'`
- `createProductBody.variants` is now optional — server logic decides
- `updateProductBody` intentionally omits `type` (immutable post-create — switching would orphan variants/options; recreate the product instead)
- `ProductDetailResponse.type` exposed

### API (`apps/api/src/products`)
- `createProduct` persists `type` and synthesizes a single default variant when `type='simple'` and no variants are provided. `variable` products are created with zero variants.
- `getProduct` and `listProducts` return `type`.

### Admin UI (`apps/admin/src/features/products`)
- New `ProductTypeCard` (RadioGroup) rendered in both create and edit modes; **disabled on edit** (the radios are locked, helper text explains why)
- Create form now submits *only* product-level fields (`type`, `name`, `handle`, `taxClassId`, `status`, `baseSku`, `categoryIds`); the server materializes the default simple variant
- Edit form:
  - `OptionsCard` shown only for variable products
  - `VariantsTable` shown for both — simple products use it to edit the single auto-created SKU's price/stock; variable products use it after generating variants from options

### Tests
- **API service tests**: new cases for default-variant auto-creation for `simple` products and zero-variant creation for `variable` products
- **Admin schema tests**: accept `simple` and `variable`, reject unknown types

## Reviewer notes

- `apps/api/src/lib/requestLogger.ts` has a pre-existing unrelated `Principal.customerId` typecheck error not introduced by this PR.
- API service tests require a live database (`apps/api/vitest.config.ts` loads `.env`); admin tests run as expected (`pnpm --filter @app/admin test` → 23 passed).
- Type immutability is enforced at the type level (`updateProductBody` has no `type` field). If we ever need to allow it, it should only be permitted while no variants exist.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `pnpm --filter @repo/database db:push` to apply the new column/enum
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @app/admin test` passes (23/23 local)
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @app/api test` passes against a fresh DB (covers `simple` auto-default and `variable` zero-variant cases)
- [ ] Manual: create a simple product → lands on edit page → variants table shows the auto-created default SKU → edit price via drawer
- [ ] Manual: create a variable product → lands on edit page → options card visible → add an option → generate variants → variants table populates
- [ ] Manual: open the edit page for an existing product → `ProductTypeCard` is visible but locked (radios disabled, helper text reads "Product type is fixed after creation")

## Summary

Hardware Task 3 milestone 3 (#396): after PHY_STREAM_OPEN binds NVCSI port A (PR #460), this PR sends the brick + CIL configuration via `CAPTURE_CSI_STREAM_SET_CONFIG_REQ` (msg id 0x40). RCE responds with `result=CAPTURE_OK` and NVCSI is now ready to receive CSI-2 packets from the wire.

## Pieces

- `kernel/include/camrtc_capture.h`: new wire-format structs ported from `docs/reference/l4t-camrtc-capture.h`:
  - `nvcsi_brick_config` (16 B) — phy_mode + lane_swizzle + per-lane polarity
  - `nvcsi_cil_config` (16 B) — num_lanes + MIPI clock rate + timing
  - `vi_hsm_csimux_error_mask_config` (8 B)
  - `nvcsi_error_config` (56 B) — HSM/LIC error routing masks
  - `capture_csi_stream_set_config_req` (104 B)
  - `capture_csi_stream_set_config_resp` (8 B)
  Plus opcode #defines (REQ=0x40, RESP=0x41) and `NVCSI_BRICK_NUM_LANES=4`.
- `kernel/drivers/camrtc/camrtc_capture.c`: `camrtc_capture_csi_stream_set_config` builds a 112-byte request frame (8-B header + 104-B body), bulk-zeroes everything (so unused error masks land at 0), then sets stream_id/csi_port/num_lanes/mipi_clock_rate. Sends via the existing IVC ring transport and validates the response opcode + transaction id.
- `kernel/tests/test_camera.c`: 11 new `_Static_assert`s pinning the brick/cil/error_config struct sizes (16/16/56), request body size (104), response size (8), field offsets for brick_config/cil_config/error_config, and opcode IDs (0x40/0x41). Catches L4T-side wire drift at build time.
- `kernel/src/shell_sys.c`: `csidiag` now chains SET_CONFIG after PHY_STREAM_OPEN with hard-coded IMX219 values (2 D-PHY lanes, 456 MHz MIPI clock — the IMX219 default link freq from `docs/reference/linux-imx219.c:139`). Skips SET_CONFIG if PHY_STREAM_OPEN doesn't return CAPTURE_OK.

## Verified on jetson-nano-1

```
slmos> csidiag
=== NVCSI port A open via RCE IVC ===
[INFO] camrtc_ivc: handshake EST/EST after kickoff
[INFO] camrtc_ivc: channel up (group=1, rx=0xbdfe1000, tx=0xbdfe6080, ...)
  capture_init:   rc=0
[INFO] phy_stream_open: send REQ tx=0x1 stream=0 port=0 phy=0
[INFO] phy_stream_open: RESP tx=0x1 result=0x0
  PHY_STREAM_OPEN: rc=0 result=0x0
[INFO] csi_stream_set_config: send REQ tx=0x2 stream=0 port=0 lanes=2 mipi_kHz=456000
[INFO] csi_stream_set_config: RESP tx=0x2 result=0x0
  CSI_SET_CONFIG:  rc=0 result=0x0
  *** NVCSI configured for IMX219 (2-lane D-PHY 456 MHz). ***
```

- [x] Static asserts validate struct/opcode sizes at build time
- [x] Deploy + `csidiag` on jetson-nano-1: PHY_STREAM_OPEN + CSI_SET_CONFIG both rc=0 result=0x0

Power on the IMX219 sensor (extend `imx219` shell command to drive `MODE_SELECT = STREAMING`) and check NVCSI `INTR_STATUS` for received packet counters. Sensor I2C CHIP_ID readback already works since PR #411.

## Summary

Phase 2-C proposal — cluster-wide KeyViz heatmaps via fan-out.

Phase 2-A and 2-B ship a heatmap that only renders the local node's view. Per parent design §5.1, reads are recorded by the follower that serves them and writes by the leader, so a single-node SPA shows a partial picture by construction. This proposal scopes a minimum-viable fan-out that ships the operator-visible value without yet requiring the proto extension parent §9.1 calls for.

## Key design decisions worth a careful read

- **Static `--keyvizFanoutNodes` flag** instead of `GetClusterOverview` discovery for the MVP (§3). The membership cache lands when clusters grow beyond hand-configured size.
- **Conservative max-merge for writes** with a `conflict` flag instead of the canonical `(bucketID, raftGroupID, leaderTerm, windowStart)` rule (§4.2). The canonical rule needs proto/JSON extensions and lands in Phase 2-C+. The MVP rule never overcounts (operators react badly to phantom hotspots) but may undercount during a leadership flip — surfaced via `conflict=true`.
- **Embedded `internal/admin` aggregator** instead of a standalone `cmd/elastickv-admin` binary (§2.2). The standalone binary was deferred indefinitely; the embedded path is the go-forward.
- **Forward-compatible wire format** (§5). Old SPA against fan-out server keeps working — the new fields are additive.

## What this proposal does NOT do

Listed in §2.2 to keep the PR-1 scope reviewable: no membership discovery, no proto extension, no standalone binary, no response caching. Each gets its own follow-up if and when needed.

## Implementation plan (per §7)

- **PR 1** — server-side aggregator + flag plumbing + table-driven test
- **PR 2** — SPA degraded banner + conflict hatching + header counter
- **PR 3 (Phase 2-C+)** — proto/JSON extension; replace max-merge with the canonical rule; promote `conflict` from per-row to per-cell

## Test plan

- [ ] Design review: confirm the §4.2 conservative max-merge trade is acceptable, or push back with the alternative (e.g., always sum + always conflict-flag if multiple nodes report > 0)
- [ ] Confirm `--keyvizFanoutNodes` flag shape (host:port list, self-included) is the right contract for now
- [ ] Confirm the timeout shape in §9 open question 2 (proposed: fixed 2 s with operator override)

body:
## Summary

Spec 003 (F-11) — share an encrypted file between two locally-registered users without revealing either party's master password.

- **`core/rsa.py`** — `RsaWrap` (RSA-OAEP-SHA256) + `RsaSign` (RSA-PSS-SHA256, MAX salt). Stateless API, every failure mode collapses to `IntegrityError` for anti-oracle uniformity.
- **`core/share_token.py`** — `.gbox-share` v1 binary container: `magic GBSH | version | sender_id | recipient_id | content_sha256 | wrapped_dek_length | wrapped_dek | expires_at | permission_flags | embedded ciphertext | RSA-PSS signature`.
- **`core/operations.share_file/accept_share`** — sender decrypts source `.crypt`, generates fresh DEK, re-encrypts with raw AES-GCM under `EMBEDDED_AAD`, wraps DEK for recipient (RSA-OAEP), signs payload (RSA-PSS), writes atomically. Recipient verifies signature **first** (anti-oracle, ADR-0015), checks recipient match, expiry, content hash, then unwraps DEK and decrypts.
- **CLI** — `guardiabox share <source.crypt> --from <sender> --to <recipient>` displays the recipient's RSA pubkey fingerprint (SHA-256, colon-hex) + `[y/N]` confirmation; `guardiabox accept <token.gbox-share> --from <sender> --as <recipient>`.
- **Bonus** — `_pattern_for_pass` non-determinism in `secure_delete.py` already shipped on main; this PR adds the hybrid RSA-share flow.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest --no-cov -q --ignore=tests/perf` — **520 tests pass** (vs 465 before Phase D = +55 tests)
  - 25 unit tests on RSA primitives (round-trip 2048+4096, byte-flip / wrong-key tampering, OAEP max payload, EC-key rejection)
  - 17 unit tests on `.gbox-share` v1 (round-trip + defensive parsing on magic/version/dek_len cap/buffer overrun)
  - 11 integration tests on share/accept (round-trip, tampered signature/payload, wrong sender pubkey, recipient mismatch, expiry, never-expires, perms, dest collide, anti-oracle ordering)
  - 5 CLI E2E tests (help smoke + Alice→Bob full flow + unknown user)
  - 3 property tests on RSA + share-token round-trips (180+ examples total)
- [x] `uv run ruff check / format / mypy --strict / bandit -ll` — all green
- [x] CI: Python 3.12 ubuntu + windows, Frontend Node 22 expected green; pre-existing CodeQL + Rust failures accepted.

## Anti-oracle proof

`tests/integration/test_share_accept.py::test_anti_oracle_signature_fails_before_expiry_check` explicitly enforces that a signed-but-expired token, byte-flipped, surfaces `IntegrityError` and **not** `ShareExpiredError` — preventing an attacker from probing token liveness via signature tampering.

## Threat model deltas

- **AD-5** (malicious recipient) is the explicit intent of the share — they receive the file and can decrypt. Cannot replay the token to a third party (DEK is wrapped under their pubkey only).
- **AD-2** (local DB tampering of recipient pubkey) is partially mitigated by the out-of-band fingerprint display + interactive confirmation.

## Module placement deviation

Plan.md spec 003 names `core.crypto.RsaWrap` and `core.crypto.RsaSign`. The implementation lives in **`core/rsa.py`** instead (CONVENTIONS §1 SRP — `core/crypto.py` already at 275 lines covering symmetric primitives). Documented in `docs/specs/003-rsa-share/tasks.md`.

body: ## Summary Когда OpenRouter возвращает абстрактное «Provider returned error», в тосте теряется конкретная причина — какой именно провайдер упал, что он сказал, какой код. Эта PR раскрывает диагностику до пользователя и в Worker-логи. Изменения в `openrouterChat()`: 1. **Обработка inline-error в HTTP 200 ответе.** OpenRouter иногда возвращает 200 + `body.error` (без `choices`), когда фритир-провайдер упал. Раньше мы воспринимали это как успех и падали на `body.choices[0].message.content` undefined, давая `empty_response` без контекста. Теперь явно проверяем `body.error` независимо от HTTP-статуса. 2. **Полная диагностика в `error`-сообщении.** Собираем `error.message`, `error.metadata.provider_name`, `error.code`, и сырой upstream-ответ из `error.metadata.raw`. Итоговый тост у пользователя выглядит как: `Rate limited [google-vertex] (code=429) — Provider quota exceeded for free tier`. 3. **`console.error` в Worker-логах** с моделью + статусом + полным body — для последующей пост-мортем-отладки если пользователь снова получит непонятную ошибку. 4. **Подсказка для empty_response**: «модель не вернула текст — попробуй другую» вместо голого `empty_response`. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human Риск: **зелёный** — изменение чисто диагностическое, не меняет бизнес-логику. - [ ] После мержа CF передеплоит за ~30 сек. - [ ] Открой дашборд → 💬 → AI-режим → выбери проблемную модель → задай вопрос. - [ ] Если модель упадёт — в тосте теперь будет вся доступная информация (имя провайдера, код, текст ошибки). Скинь скриншот тоста — по нему сразу будет понятно нужен ли пополнить баланс / переключить модель / репортить OpenRouter. - [ ] Если хочешь самостоятельно копать — включи **Logs** в CF Workers → Observability → задай AI-вопрос → в логах будет полный JSON ответа OpenRouter (полезно для понимания что там реально пришло). ### Notes - Не зависит от PR #11 (обновление списка моделей) — можно мерджить параллельно или после. - В будущем стоит добавить автоматический retry с другой моделью если первая упала с 5xx — но это отдельная фича. ## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

## Summary

Upgrade the preview URL generation formula from v2 (`${projectSlug}-${branchSlug}`) to v3 (`${tail}-${prefix}-${projectSlug}`), placing the most important information (what the branch does) first, followed by the agent/type prefix, then the project name. This improves UX by making branch purpose immediately visible in the URL.

Additionally, fix a critical bug where non-legacy projects would enter a refresh-rebuild loop when accessed via bare-slug subdomains, by implementing three-tier fallback resolution in the proxy.

## Key Changes

- **New module `cds/src/services/preview-slug.ts`**: Single source of truth for preview slug computation
  - `slugifyForPreview()`: Normalizes strings to DNS-friendly slugs (lowercase, non-alphanumeric→hyphen, collapse/trim hyphens)
  - `computePreviewSlug(branch, projectSlug)`: Generates v3 slugs by splitting branch on first `/` (prefix/tail) and composing as `${tail}-${prefix}-${projectSlug}`
  - Handles edge cases: no prefix (main branch), multi-level paths, empty components

- **Updated `cds/src/services/comment-template.ts`**: 
  - `buildPreviewUrl()` now takes three parameters: `host`, `branch` (original with `/`), `projectSlug`
  - Uses `computePreviewSlug()` internally to generate v3 URLs
  - Becomes the single entry point for all preview URL generation across the codebase

- **Fixed proxy routing in `cds/src/services/proxy.ts`**:
  - New `resolveBranchEntry()` method implements three-tier fallback:
    1. **v3 forward match** (primary): Iterate all entries, compute their v3 slug, match against input
    2. **v1 compatibility**: Direct lookup by bare slug (legacy projects)
    3. **v2 compatibility**: Lookup by `${project.slug}-${slug}` (ceb2c01 era links)
  - Prevents non-legacy projects from triggering auto-build on every reload when accessed via bare-slug subdomains
  - `routeToBranch()` now uses `resolveBranchEntry()` instead of direct state lookup

- **Enhanced transit page HTML** (`cds/src/index.ts`):
  - Redesigned "preparing preview" page with improved visual hierarchy
  - Added CSS custom properties for dark/light theme support (`:root` + `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)`)
  - Timeline-style step indicators with pulse animation for running state
  - Collapsible log section (hidden by default to avoid noise)
  - "Go to preview" button + helpful hint instead of auto-refresh countdown
  - Proper HTML escaping for branch names to prevent injection

- **Updated all URL generation call sites**:
  - `cds/src/routes/branches.ts`: Smoke test uses `buildPreviewUrl()`
  - `cds/src/routes/github-webhook.ts`: PR comments use `buildPreviewUrl()`
  - `cds/src/routes/comment-template.ts`: Settings preview uses `buildPreviewUrl()`
  - `cds/src/services/check-run-runner.ts`: Check-run summaries use `buildPreviewUrl()`
  - `cds/web/app.js`: Dashboard preview button reads `previewSlug` from branch data

- **Comprehensive test coverage**:
  - `cds/tests/services/preview-slug.test.ts`: 20+ tests for slug computation (edge cases, consistency, uniqueness)
  - `cds/tests/services/proxy.test.ts`: 5 new tests for three-tier resolution (v3 match, v1/v2 compatibility, fallback to auto-build)
  - `cds/tests/services/comment-template.test.ts`: Updated tests for v3 URL format
  - `cds/tests/routes/branches-smoke.test.ts`: Updated smoke test expectations

- **Documentation updates**:
  - `.claude/skills/

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches CDS preview routing and URL generation across webhook comments, check-runs, dashboard, and proxy resolution; mistakes could break preview links or trigger unintended auto-builds, though changes include compatibility fallbacks and added tests.

> **Overview**

author: bingqinglyu
body:
## Problem

LLMs (especially Gemini) can enter self-reinforcing text generation loops where they repeatedly emit the same patterns without invoking any tools. For example:

```
Wait, I should check item 1... Done. Sent.
Wait, I should check item 2... Done. Sent.
Wait, I should check item 3... Done. Sent.
... (repeats indefinitely until token limit)
```

The existing `tool-loop-detection` module only monitors tool calls. When a model loops in pure text output, there is currently **no detection or abort mechanism**, causing:
- Token/cost waste (entire context window consumed by repetition)
- User-facing message spam
- Session becoming unrecoverable

## Related Issues

- #25627 — Coder agent repeats messages on exec running retries (text repetition aspect)
- #24800 — Context overflow from undetected loops
- #40396 — Agent trapped in infinite thought loop after upgrade

## Solution

Add a `text-repetition-guard` module that detects streaming text-generation loops using four complementary strategies:

1. **N-gram frequency** — Detects repeated phrases via sliding window
2. **Consecutive identical lines** — Catches copy-paste style repetition
3. **Suffix cycle detection** — Identifies repeating tail patterns
4. **Line-group cycle detection** — Catches multi-line block repetition

The guard is integrated into `handleMessageUpdate` and runs every `checkIntervalChars` characters (default: 200). On detection, it sets an `abortedByTextRepetitionGuard` flag and calls `session.abort()`.

### Key implementation details

- **Config** integrated into standard `ToolsConfig` / `AgentToolsConfig` system
- **Resolved config cached** at message start (zero per-tick resolution overhead)
- **False-positive mitigations**: degenerate content filtering, progressive content detection (e.g. "Step 1..., Step 2..."), n-gram source-line diversity check
- **blockChunker drain prevention**: When the guard fires, a state flag prevents `handleMessageEnd` from draining buffered repetitive content (addresses Greptile review feedback)

## Tests

15 test cases covering all 4 detection strategies, edge cases, progressive content (no false positive), and configuration.

## What

Adds `friend_list` to the agent's notes/friend tools. Lists known friends with id, name, trust level, and external-id pairs. Optional trust filter and limit.

## Why

The notes/friend repertoire had:

| | tool | scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read | `get_friend_note` | one friend by id |
| write | `save_friend_note` | update one friend |
| _missing_ | enumerate | — |

Real workflows that needed it:
- cross-chat outreach decisions: "who do I know on this channel?"
- screener triage: "is this sender already a friend?"
- orienting at session start: "remind me who's family"

## How

```
friend_list(trust?, limit?)
```

Reads `ctx.friendStore.listAll()` (already exists on `FileFriendStore`; interface optional). Filters by trust level if given (defaulting `undefined` trustLevel to "friend" so older records aren't dropped). Sorts alphabetically by `name`. Slices to `limit` (1-200, default 50).

Renders:
```
3 friends with trust=family:
- ari-mendelow (family): Ari [imessage-handle:+15555550000, email:ari@mendelow.me]
- jordan-lee (family): Jordan
- sam-park (family): Sam
```

Empty-state is filter-aware:
- no filter, empty store → "no friends recorded yet."
- filter set, no matches → "no friends with trust level 'family'."

Defensive handling:
- no `friendStore` → "i can't list friends -- friend store not available"
- `friendStore` without `listAll` → "the configured friend store does not support listing."

## Tests

4 new tests in `tools-notes-friend.test.ts`:
- 3 friends, sorted alphabetically (Aria < Bea < Cleo)
- trust filter on `family` returns only family-trust entries; non-family excluded
- store without `listAll` returns the "does not support listing" message
- filter that matches nothing returns the filter-aware empty message

11/11 notes-friend tests pass.

Tool registry: 74 → 75. H10 contract list updated, snapshot regenerated.

## Notes

- This kicks off the second round of the diagnostic + tooling cluster (round 1: #615-#634). Same pattern: small surface, family-trust-aware, structured output, defensive against missing optional capabilities.

## Summary

Addresses the FOD-determinism issue (#7). Two-commit fix:

1. **`fix(nix): rotate mixFodDeps hash`** — accept today's deterministic output hash (`sha256-i11gJiWjgoCcKRIt0ePjMQOqXTJIVEETQv4s75pEpNU=`).
2. **`docs(nix): explain mixFodDeps optional-dep resolution fragility`** — colocate a maintenance recipe comment at the `mixFodDeps` invocation site so the next person hitting this drift gets the context without walking the issue tracker.

The architect-recommended option-A+ "force lockfile-driven resolution" step simplified to a no-op for this PR: I ran `mix deps.get` via `nix shell nixpkgs#beam27Packages.elixir_1_19 nixpkgs#git` and got **zero changes** to `mix.lock` against today's hex registry state. So the lockfile-pin commit isn't needed right now — Mix's resolver correctly excludes the previously-fetched rustler optional dep, producing deterministic output bytes against the existing lockfile. The maintenance recipe (in commit 2's docstring) lays out what to do if drift recurs in either direction.

## Root cause (verified)

`mix.lock` has no `rustler` entry. 9 packages declare `{:rustler, ..., optional: true}`. Mix's `deps.get` resolver consults the live hex registry when deciding whether to fetch optional transitive deps that aren't lockfile-pinned, and that decision can flip on registry-state changes. Apr 15's run fetched rustler 0.37.3; Apr 27's skipped it. Same lockfile, different FOD output bytes.

Independently verified via architect-level review:
- Input invariance: `mix.lock` and `flake.lock` byte-identical between hash-record commit (`01c3385`, 2026-04-15) and HEAD; resolution-relevant slice of `mix.exs` byte-identical.
- Diff: only `rustler/` directory differs between the two cached output paths (`bxzccgd...` with rustler/ → OLD hash; `xlf67d1...` without → NEW hash).
- Ruled out alternatives: nixpkgs `fetch-mix-deps.nix` drift, siwe-ex git packing variation, `.hex` format changes.

Architect explicitly rejected `mix2nix` (option B) — same root cause would apply unless the lockfile already pins the optional, at which point the lockfile fix IS the cure.

## Test plan

- [x] `nix build .#default` succeeds end-to-end on a fresh sandbox with the new hash.
- [x] `bin/blockscout` (the mixRelease entrypoint) runs against the rotated FOD without errors related to missing deps.
- [x] `mix.lock` byte-identical pre/post the `mix deps.get` run today (no lockfile delta needed).
- [ ] CI green on this PR.
- [ ] Downstream: `klazomenai/autonity-blockscout-nixos` `chore(deps)` PR bumping the `blockscout.url` rev to this PR's merge commit. Then PR #20 there can rebase + go green on the FOD step.

## Out of scope

- The downstream `RELEASE_COOKIE` wiring bug surfaced in the same VM-test run is a `klazomenai/autonity-blockscout-nixos` consumer-side bug (the `mixRelease` `removeCookie = true` default is deliberate per upstream nixpkgs convention; consumer is expected to set `RELEASE_COOKIE` env). Separate issue + fix on the glue repo.

Refs #7
